title: JSON in and out, validation and standardised errors

videos.script: boxoffice still answers in tab-separated text. This lesson makes it speak JSON, in both directions. {{out}} Writing JSON is the easy half. Encode first, then send, so a failure can still be an honest 500. {{in}} Reading JSON is the hard half, because the body comes from a stranger. You will send seven broken bodies, and get seven different answers. Empty, truncated, too big, a field nobody asked for. {{valid}} Then the next question. The JSON parsed, but does it make sense? Forty tickets, or zero, or an e-mail with no at sign. That is validation, and it lives beside the handler. {{problem}} Every refusal gets one shape, the problem details of RFC 9457. And one catch-all route shows how a tidy 404 can cost you an honest 405. {{store}} Last, the store learns to say no in its own words. Sold out is not an HTTP error. One small function turns it into a 409.
